An original instrumental piece of music for a calm, thoughtful science-fiction strategy game set among the real nearby stars. About two and a half minutes long. Cinematic but restrained, spacious and warm, mixed to sit quietly under a game: no sudden loud hits, no build-ups to a big drop. It begins softly and ends by fading gently to silence. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no humming, no spoken words, no choir.

Patient, ancient and communal music for a settlement of an invented people who live in the endless dusk of a world that never turns. Very slow, about 56 BPM, in E Dorian. A low bowed drone like a deep string held for a long time, soft resonant frame drums struck slowly and far apart, a wooden flute with a breathy tone playing a long, unhurried melody, plucked strings answering it now and then, warm and a little mysterious; it never hurries, and the dusk never ends.

The main theme. Slow, about 70 BPM, in D major. [0:00 - 0:30] a soft bed of synthesiser pads and a distant low string drone; [0:30 - 1:30] a clear, memorable melody on solo French horn, answered by strings, growing to a hopeful, wide statement with the full string section and gentle timpani; [1:30 - 2:30] the melody returns softly on piano over the pads, and the piece settles and fades.

Warm, wide and calm music for the end of a long journey that has been won. Slow, about 68 BPM, in D major. Soft synthesiser pads and a low string drone open it; a broad, singing melody on solo French horn and then the full strings rises to a warm, generous statement with gentle timpani rolls, then settles onto piano and pads and fades. Tense, grave music for a time of war, felt from far away rather than in the thick of battle. Slow, about 66 BPM, in C minor. A low, steady pulse on muted timpani and deep synthesiser, taut low strings playing short repeated figures, muted French horns holding long, uneasy chords, a slow build in the middle that never breaks into a climax, then a return to the low pulse. Serious and watchful, never triumphant or martial.
